summary: Henrique Galvão (1895–1970) was an officer, colonial administrator and writer who turned against the Estado Novo after a 1947 report to the National Assembly described forced labour in Angola in terms the regime would not accept. Imprisoned, he escaped from custody in 1959 and took refuge in Latin America. In January 1961 he led the seizure of the liner Santa Maria in the Caribbean, holding it for eleven days to force the world's press to attend to the dictatorship — an operation that succeeded as publicity and coincided, weeks later, with the outbreak of the war in Angola. He is in the atlas as the clearest case of opposition from inside the colonial administration itself.
